sections.name: Hell knight
sections.card:
Summary: A tough monster that throws green fireballs from a distance and claws you up close. It has 500 hit points, and in Doom 64 it is less pale than the standard Hell knight and looks more like the baron of Hell.
Weak points: It rarely flinches, so the rocket launcher, plasma gun and super shotgun are the best answers, and the chaingun and shotgun also work at close range. Do not fight it in melee: it claws back, and the chainsaw is ineffective against it.
Tips: Its fireballs are faster than an imp's or a cacodemon's and hit hard, but from a distance you can dodge them without much trouble. In Doom 64 Hell knights and barons of Hell can hurt each other with their fireballs, so infighting between the two is possible.

sections.name: Baron of Hell
sections.card:
Summary: One of the toughest monsters in the game, with 1000 hit points; it claws up close and throws fireballs from a distance. In Doom 64 it is red-orange and throws red fireballs, and the green colour goes to the Hell knight instead.
Weak points: It rarely flinches, so use the rocket launcher, plasma gun or super shotgun. The chaingun and shotgun also work if you can stay at a distance, but they take a while. Melee is risky because you can be clawed.
Tips: Its fireballs are not too hard to dodge when you have room, especially by circle-strafing, but in a confined space it is much more dangerous. In Doom 64 barons and Hell knights hurt each other with their fireballs and so can end up fighting each other.

sections.name: Mancubus
sections.card:
Summary: A slow, wide monster with flamethrower arms that spits fireballs in bursts. In Doom 64 it is taller, wears a metal harness with a fuel pack on its back, and its fireballs are smaller and look like fiery brimstone. It first appears in MAP09: Even Simpler.
Weak points: It is slow and a big target, so rapid-fire weapons kill it easily, and the rocket launcher is possibly the most effective weapon against it. It pauses and gives a battle cry before it fires, so even a slow weapon such as the super shotgun can stun it out of attacking.
Tips: Keep your distance: up close you may take two fireballs instead of one. Once it starts attacking it keeps firing until all three bursts are done, even if you step out of its sight, unless you hurt it mid-burst; you can use that to start monster infighting. In Doom 64 the direction of its fireballs is somewhat different from Doom II.

sections.name: Arachnotron
sections.card:
Summary: A cybernetic brain on a big metal spider body. In Doom 64 it has two plasma guns that fire two blue bolts at once in spurts of five, and it keeps firing as long as it can see you. It first appears in MAP14: Eye of the Storm, unless you play the secret levels MAP30: The Lair and MAP32: Hectic first, which also hold some.
Weak points: It has a medium pain chance, so rapid-fire weapons such as the chaingun work well. Do not use the chainsaw on it: its size stops the attack reliably connecting.
Tips: Its plasma bursts are among the fastest projectiles around and its high rate of fire can drain your health quickly. Keep attacking, move in broad side-to-side steps and slip out of its line of fire now and then, and you will take little damage. In monster infighting the Doom 64 version often beats even a baron of Hell, but with little health left.

sections.name: Cacodemon
sections.card:
Summary: A floating monster with a big mouth that spits balls of lightning and bites. In Doom 64 it is beige-brown with a single yellow-green eye and two arms with broken chains, and it swings its arms as it flies.
Weak points: It is slow and flinches easily, so repeating weapons such as the chaingun or the plasma gun push it away until it can barely fight back. The chainsaw can also stun it.
Tips: Its shots are fairly easy to dodge, and with enough room you can fight several at once and take little or no damage. Once alerted it can come flying out of unexpected places. On the Nintendo 64 its shots fly faster than on PC, though the cacodemon itself still moves slowly.

sections.name: Pain elemental
sections.card:
Summary: A floating monster that spits lost souls at you instead of firing a shot. In Doom 64 it is dark pink with a green eye and two mouths in place of arms, so it can spawn two lost souls at the same time, and it gives a low sinister laugh when it spots you.
Weak points: Focus on the pain elemental itself and leave its lost souls until it is dead. Fast-firing weapons such as the chaingun or the plasma gun work fairly well and usually keep the lost souls at bay. The rocket launcher is not recommended, because it may spit a lost soul while your rocket is in flight, and the blast can hurt you.
Tips: Do not stand at point-blank range to stop it spawning, as you could in other versions: in Doom 64 every lost soul that fails to appear, including the ones it spawns when it dies, explodes with damage like an exploding barrel, and two together are roughly a rocket hit. It only spawns lost souls while you are in its line of sight, so hit it hard, then head for cover.

sections.name: Cyberdemon
sections.card:
Summary: A towering demon with a rocket launcher for an arm and 4000 hit points. In Doom 64 it has darker skin and is much larger than on PC, and its rockets leave smoke trails. It is rare, appearing chiefly in the secret levels or late in the game.
Weak points: The BFG9000 is the most effective weapon against it, and the plasma gun works fairly well. The rocket launcher also works, but it is a long fight, and rockets must hit it directly because it takes no blast damage. Other weapons and melee take far longer, so avoid them.
Tips: It rarely flinches, so you cannot easily stop it attacking: circle-strafe and avoid every rocket, because one will often badly hurt you. In Doom 64 its rockets are faster and come out of the launcher itself, so they head downward at you and can burst on the floor near you, even when no wall is close. On the Watch Me Die skill level, MAP17: Watch Your Step ends with two cyberdemons and MAP24: No Escape has three.

sections.name: Lost soul
sections.card:
Summary: A flaming flying skull that charges at you with open jaws. In Doom 64 it has black horns and an open skull with fire only on top, and it recovers from each attack much faster than on PC. It attacks viciously, which makes it one of the most dangerous enemies in Doom 64.
Weak points: It is weaker than on PC: a single shotgun blast can fell it. You can stop a charge by shooting it while it is attacking, and a chaingun is useful against a crowd, because a shot lost soul becomes helpless until it hits something.
Tips: It is completely silent when it spots you, so the hissing breath as it launches is often the first warning. Do not use rockets on a group: a lost soul may suddenly fly at you and make a rocket blow up close enough to hurt you. They are more often found in groups than alone.

sections.name: Demon and spectre
sections.card:
Summary: Fast monsters that only attack up close. Doom 64's manual calls the demon the bull demon; it has black horns, small red eyes, bigger teeth and claws, and a slightly longer melee reach than on PC. The spectre is the same kind of monster, but in Doom 64 it starts as an opaque green-tinted demon and turns see-through once it spots you.
Weak points: They have no ranged attack, so they are no threat at long range. The super shotgun can kill a demon at close range with one blast, a shotgun used hit-and-run works too, and the chaingun is also effective. The chainsaw stops a demon attacking while you saw it, and uses no ammo.
Tips: They run fast and in a zig-zag, closing distance quickly and helping to corner you. Lure them into a tight corridor so they cannot swarm you from all directions, and use the chainsaw there. They are generally the easiest monsters to trick into attacking other enemies.

sections.name: Chainsaw
sections.card:
Summary: A melee weapon that saws anything in reach, roughly a quadruple-speed fist, and it uses no ammo. The Doom 64 version has two blades and the letters U.A.C. engraved on top, and does roughly double the damage of the PC one.
Uses: Best against demons and spectres, which you can usually kill without taking damage, and fairly effective against cacodemons and imps. Its rapid fire works well on enemies that flinch easily, because it keeps them from hitting back. It is ineffective against Hell knights and other demons with powerful attacks and low pain chance.
Tips: Its reach is only 65 map units, barely more than a fist's 64, so you have to be right on top of the target. Against a pack of demons, back into a corner and saw them down one by one. In open areas with several enemies it is a liability, because it kills more slowly than a berserk fist.

sections.name: BFG9000
sections.card:
Summary: The ultimate weapon: it fires a big ball of green plasma that can destroy nearly any monster in one shot and spreads damage over a wide area. In Doom 64 it has a darker colour scheme and first turns up in MAP10: The Bleeding.
Uses: Good for clearing a room. The plasma ball explodes where it hits, and a moment later invisible rays fan out in a cone from you and hurt what they hit. Even cyberdemons, which are immune to blast damage, are hurt by those rays.
Tips: It does not fire the instant you pull the trigger: in Doom 64 there is a wait of exactly one second before the ball leaves, and the rays follow about half a second after it hits. The rays go in the direction the ball was fired even if you turn, so keep facing your target. A shot takes 40 cells, and a BFG you pick up holds 40.

sections.name: Megasphere
sections.card:
Summary: A gray-brown orb that sets both your health and your armour to 200 percent; the armour is the same as blue armour. In Doom 64 it shows a helmet like the player's instead of a demonic face.
Uses: One pickup tops up both health and armour at once. It counts in the items percentage shown at the end of each level.
Tips: The first one in Doom 64 is in MAP06: Alpha Quadrant, and the game holds nine or ten of them, depending on the skill level.

sections.name: Super shotgun
sections.card:
Summary: The double-barrelled sawed-off shotgun: two shells per shot and 20 pellets per blast, about three times as damaging as the normal shotgun per shot. In Doom 64 it reloads much faster, in 1.53 seconds against 1.77 in Doom II, and it knocks you back a little when fired. It is one of the most essential weapons in Doom 64.
Uses: One well-aimed blast almost always kills two imps, one demon or one spectre. It lets you hold your own against tough monsters such as Hell knights, arachnotrons and mancubi, and it is often a better choice than the rocket launcher there, because shells are more plentiful than rockets and a short-range rocket blast can hurt you.
Tips: The pellets spread wide, even up and down, so it is wasteful at long range: switch to the shotgun to snipe, or to deal with a lone enemy in a maze. It uses the same shells as the shotgun.

sections.name: Plasma gun
sections.card:
Summary: A rapid-fire gun that shoots bursts of blue plasma and shares your energy cells with the BFG9000. In Doom 64 it has a blue electric tube on top that buzzes constantly.
Uses: It is devastating against nearly any single enemy and can be considered the game's jack-of-all-trades. A continuous barrage stops an arachnotron or a mancubus in its tracks and can slow a baron of Hell to about half its normal speed and attack rate.
Tips: In Doom 64 it fires a little slower than on PC, one shot every 0.133 seconds, but there is no pause after you let go of the trigger and the shots travel faster. At long range enemies tend to move too much for a burst to hit, so fire in controlled bursts rather than holding the trigger.

sections.name: Berserk pack
sections.card:
Summary: A dark gray medikit that raises your health to 100 percent if it was lower and makes your punches far stronger. It also fills the screen with a red haze, which lasts only three seconds in Doom 64.
Uses: It makes your punch ten times stronger, usually until the level ends or you die: enough to smash humanoids to a pulp, or sometimes kill a demon in one blow. Your current weapon switches to the fist when you pick it up, so you can end up suddenly unarmed.
Tips: The extra strength does not run out when the red haze fades, so do not stop punching because the screen has cleared. Use it hit-and-run: run up, punch, then retreat or dodge. A punch does not latch on like the chainsaw, so aim carefully.
